sections.html:
Tooele County spreads across 7,286 square miles of northwestern Utah, 6,941 of them land, just west of Salt Lake County. Nearly everyone lives along the eastern edge. Tooele had 35,742 residents in 2020, Grantsville 12,617, the unincorporated community of Stansbury Park 9,851 and Wendover, on the Nevada line, 1,115. The whole county held 72,698 people in 2020, compared with 40,735 in 2000.

A town lot in Tooele and acreage at the desert's edge can carry the same county mailing address yet be valued separately by the assessor.

Owners in Stansbury Park have one more layer. The community started in 1970 as a planned development around a golf course and a man-made lake. Its water and sewer service comes from the Stansbury Park Improvement District, and the Stansbury Park Community Association signs off in preliminary form on housing and remodeling plans. Expect buyers there to ask about association rules before anything else.

Each parcel is valued on January 1, and payment is on time through November 30.

DateStep in the tax year
January 1Valuation date for every parcel
May 22Assessor finishes the roll and certifies values to the Auditor
May or JuneTax sale of parcels delinquent more than five years
July or AugustNotices of valuation mailed
August or SeptemberBoard of Equalization hears appeals, 45 days from mailing
By November 1Tax notices mailed
November 30Final day to pay with no penalty
December 1Unpaid balances turn delinquent

Current dates are posted on the assessor dates page. For questions, call the Treasurer's office at (435) 843-3190 or stop by 47 S. Main Street in Tooele on a weekday between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm.

sections.h2: Winter and desert wear on a house
sections.html:
Summers run hot and dry, and winters are cold and snowy. January highs normally reach 38.7 degrees and July highs 91.4. A year in Tooele brings about 18.44 inches of precipitation and 75.3 inches of snow, and temperatures have ranged from 106 degrees to minus 16. Wendover gets only about 4.58 inches of precipitation.

Buyers' inspectors in this county go to the roof, furnace and water heater first, then look for settling and bad grading around the foundation. A house left empty for a few winters shows more damage. Selling as-is hands those repairs to the buyer.

Your filing window with the county Board of Equalization lasts 45 days from the day your Notice of Property Valuation was mailed, or through September 15.

The board wants at least one of these four kinds of proof:

  • Comparable sales of similar homes that closed before January 1 at less than your assessed value.
  • A closing statement for a purchase made before January 1. Short sales, bank-owned sales and foreclosures also need the bank's required appraisal.
  • An appraisal whose effective date falls within the year.
  • A written description of a factual mistake, such as the wrong square footage or a carport recorded as a garage.

A high bill alone will not win a reduction. Rates come out of public budget hearings held by cities, school districts and other districts, and the board looks at value. Still unhappy with the ruling? Put your appeal to the State Tax Commission in writing and file it through the county auditor within 30 days. A typical homeowner saves $4 to $8 in tax for every $1,000 of value removed, and the Tax Commission's appeals publication lays out the process.

sections.h2: Primary residential exemption and a sale
sections.html:
A home that qualifies as a primary residence is taxed on 55 percent of market value. That break stays with the seller and does not transfer to the next owner.

Each residential unit can claim it for up to one acre, as long as the home is lived in as a primary residence, and part-year use counts if it adds up to at least 183 consecutive days. Households get one. A buyer applies on Form TC-473A, emailed to assessorsurvey@tooeleco.gov. If nothing comes back within 30 days, the county sends a notice giving 30 more days, after which the exemption comes off.

A rule change begins January 1, 2027 under 2026 SB 238: any transfer of an ownership interest, deeds and trust transfers included, requires a new form, with applications due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. Without the exemption, tax is figured on 100 percent of market value. Heirs and landlords who plan to sell a rental in Tooele County should plan for this before listing.

December 1 is when an unpaid bill becomes delinquent and penalty and interest begin to pile up. A parcel more than five years behind is eligible for the tax sale. The penalty has opened at the greater of 1 percent or $10, then climbed to the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 once January 31 passes, and interest has been 10 percent on the balance owed December 1. Get the current numbers from the Treasurer.

The Auditor advertises the tax sale once a week for four weeks, and owners may redeem before it happens. If you are behind and ready to move on, contact us before the delinquency list is published. We request the payoff from the Treasurer and schedule the closing to match it.

sections.h2: Selling a house with back taxes
sections.html:
Owing tax may slow a sale but will not kill it. The county's lien outranks most other claims, so the title company pays it at closing, usually from what you would receive. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff that holds through your planned closing day. Several open years generally all need to be cleared.

Collect the deed, the newest tax notice and the valuation notice. With a rental or an empty house, confirm that mail reached the right address, since a missing notice is a frequent cause of back taxes. We work with houses in any Tooele County town, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park. A cash purchase gets around the problem by paying the balance through closing.

sections.h2: A timeline for owners planning to sell
sections.html:
Timing your sale around the tax year saves trouble. In summer, look for your valuation notice and decide whether a filing is worth the effort before the board's window closes. In autumn, watch for the tax notice and pay it, or confirm that your mortgage servicer has. If you list after November 30, the year's tax is already due, and the title company will divide it between you and the buyer on the settlement statement.

Anyone carrying several years of back tax is better off closing before a May or June tax sale. In every case, a call to the Treasurer a few days before closing confirms what the payoff should be.

Bills, payments and delinquencies belong to the Treasurer, 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, (435) 843-3190. Value, the primary residence form and appeals belong to the assessor's office. Work out which one you need before driving over, and keep the parcel number handy.

faqs.q: When are Tooele County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 and there is no penalty on the year's real property tax. A balance left after that is delinquent from December 1. Notices are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Tooele County property valuation?
faqs.a: Whichever comes later: September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice was mailed. Take your filing to the county Board of Equalization with comparable sales, an appraisal, a closing statement or proof of a factual error.

faqs.q: Do I lose the 45 percent residential exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, as the seller. After the sale the new owner has to apply separately, and without an approved application the property can be taxed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Where is the Tooele County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's office is at 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, and answers at (435) 843-3190. Open weekdays, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

faqs.q: Can you buy a Tooele County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. We ask the Treasurer for the current balance and pay it through closing. Houses in any Tooele County town qualify, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.
